mainKeyword: cordless power tool combo kit under 500
guideTitle: Best Cordless Tool Combo Kits Under $500 (2026)
metaDescription: Five cordless power tool combo kits at or under $500 from Milwaukee, DEWALT, CRAFTSMAN and HART compared on tool mix, motors, battery count and platform.
expertTake: The Milwaukee 2695-24 M18 kit is the pick for most buyers because a hammer drill, an impact driver, a Hackzall reciprocating saw and a work light sit on a platform that scales to hundreds of tools. The DEWALT 5-tool kit is the value pick for a household that wants brushless drilling and a circular saw in one bag. Skip a big multi-tool kit if you will only ever use the drill and the impact driver, because the spare tools and batteries are what you pay extra for. The extra budget over a basic kit mostly buys brushless motors, a bigger battery and a broader platform.
introParagraphs: A cordless combo kit bundles several tools around a shared battery, which makes the first tool purchase cheap and locks you into a platform for the next ten years. The count of tools on the box matters less than which tools are included, whether they are brushless, and how many batteries you get.

This guide explains what the upper end of a larger budget buys in a combo kit, how tool mix and motor type change the real value, and where a long tool count hides weak batteries. The picks are listed above, with the reviews below. Listing prices move, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Milwaukee 2695-24 M18 4-Tool Kit: Hammer Drill, Impact Driver, Hackzall, Light
products.description:
A hammer drill adds a tapping action for masonry, so one tool drills wood, steel and brick anchors, which is an advantage over the plain drills in several other kits. The impact driver drives lag bolts through thick lumber, and the Hackzall is a one-handed reciprocating saw that cuts branches, lumber and PVC. A work light rounds out the kit, so you have lighting on a dark job.

The real value is the M18 platform. Milwaukee builds hundreds of tools on the same battery, from saws and grinders to vacuums and lights, so a kit like this is the start of a collection, not the end. Compared with the DEWALT 5-tool kit, the Milwaukee has fewer tools but a pro-focused hammer drill. Compared with the CRAFTSMAN 7-tool kit, it gives you fewer pieces and stronger ones.

Ownership: batteries are the long-term cost, so buy a larger pack when you can. Keep the chucks clean, oil the Hackzall's shoe pivot and store batteries cool. The tools are brushed or brushless depending on the model, so check the version before assuming runtime.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a pro-grade platform and plan to add tools over the years.
pros: Hammer drill handles masonry anchors as well as wood and steel
Hackzall one-handed saw suits tight spaces and pruning
M18 platform spans hundreds of compatible tools
Work light adds usability in dark spaces
cons: Fewer tools than the DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN kits
Motor type depends on the tool version in the kit

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX 5-Tool Combo Kit with Brushless Drill and Impact Driver
products.description:
A brushless motor delivers 340 unit watts out, DEWALT's measure of power at the chuck, so the drill is a step above the brushed drills in lower-tier kits. The impact driver is the compact DCF787 with 1,500 in-lbs of torque, and the kit adds a compact reciprocating saw and a circular saw that cover demolition and framing cuts. With five tools, it covers drilling, driving, cutting and sawing in one bag.

The tradeoff is that a five-tool kit stretches the batteries. Compared with the Milwaukee kit, you get more tools but not a hammer drill. Compared with the DEWALT drill and circular saw kit, you get an impact driver and a reciprocating saw for a modest step up. For a homeowner who wants one kit for every job, it is a sensible choice.

Ownership: carry a spare battery for long jobs, because a circular saw drains compact packs quickly. Keep the saws' blade guards clean and replace blades when they dull. Store batteries cool and partly charged, and use the bag to keep tools together.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want brushless drilling plus saws in one complete kit.
pros: Brushless drill delivers 340 UWO and long runtime
Impact driver provides 1,500 in-lbs of torque
Compact reciprocating saw fits between studs
Five tools cover most household projects
cons: Compact batteries drain quickly under the circular saw
Larger kit costs more than a two-tool kit

products.name: HART 20-Volt 4-Tool Brushless Combo Kit with 2.0Ah and 4.0Ah Batteries
products.description:
A 4.0Ah battery lasts twice as long as a 2.0Ah pack, and this kit includes one of each, so you have a compact pack for light work and a large one for heavy jobs. All four tools in the kit are described as brushless, which brings the runtime and cool operation of premium kits to a lower tier. The platform is HART's 20V line.

The tradeoff is the platform and the brand's track record. HART is newer than DEWALT or Milwaukee, so the tool range and long-term support are less proven. Compared with the CRAFTSMAN kit, the HART gives you brushless tools but fewer of them. For a buyer who wants brushless performance without a premium price, it is a smart choice.

Ownership: check what the four tools are before buying, because kits vary by listing. Keep batteries cool and partly charged. Because the platform is smaller, make sure the tools you want later exist in the HART line before committing.
products.bestFor: Budget-minded buyers who want brushless tools and a larger battery in the kit.
pros: All four tools are brushless for longer runtime
Includes both a 2.0Ah and a 4.0Ah battery
Lower relative price for a brushless kit
Four tools cover the core jobs
cons: Platform is newer and narrower than the big brands

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 CMCK700D2 7-Tool Cordless Combo Kit with 2 Batteries
products.description:
Seven tools in one kit is the largest set here, and it covers drilling, driving, cutting, sanding and lighting. The drill delivers 280 unit watts out with a two-speed gearbox, a respectable figure for a consumer drill. The kit includes two batteries, a charger and accessories, so it is a complete starter workshop in a box.

The tradeoff is that more tools usually means less depth in each. Compared with the Milwaukee kit, the CRAFTSMAN's tools are lighter duty, and compared with the DEWALT kit, they are not brushless in the drill's listing. The V20 platform has a decent tool range, but it is narrower than M18 or 20V MAX. For a homeowner who wants every tool in one purchase, the tool count is the draw.

Ownership: with two batteries for seven tools, expect to swap often during big projects. Keep each tool's accessories organized in the bag. Check that you actually need all seven tools, since each is another item to store.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Brushless Drill Driver and Circular Saw Kit, 2 x 2Ah

specList.label: Saw
specList.value: Cordless circular saw with bevel capacity

products.description:
A brushless drill driver and a bevel-capable circular saw are the two tools most DIY projects need, and this kit packages them with two batteries and a contractor bag. The drill is described as having a lightweight build and an ergonomic grip, and the saw makes aggressive bevel cuts. Two 2.0Ah batteries keep one charging while the other works.

The tradeoff is breadth. With only two tools, you will need to buy an impact driver and other tools separately, and the 2.0Ah batteries are small for a circular saw. Compared with the DEWALT 5-tool kit, this one is simpler and cheaper but less complete. For someone who builds decks and shelves, the drill and saw cover the main jobs.

Ownership: consider upgrading one battery to a 5.0Ah pack for saw work. Keep the saw's blade guard clean, and use a sharp blade to reduce battery drain. The contractor bag keeps tools and batteries together.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A drill and impact driver cover most work, and a circular saw or reciprocating saw adds cutting. The Milwaukee kit adds a hammer drill and Hackzall, the DEWALT 5-tool kit adds both saws and the CRAFTSMAN kit includes seven tools. A kit with tools you will not use is a poor value. List the jobs you do before choosing. Write down the last five projects you did and count how often each tool would have been used before you pay for a long tool list.

Brushless motors give longer runtime and a longer life. The HART kit lists all four tools as brushless, the DEWALT kits list brushless drills and the CRAFTSMAN drill is not stated brushless. For weekly use, brushless pays back. Ask also whether the listing names each tool's model, since kits sometimes mix a brushless drill with a brushed saw.

A 2.0Ah pack lasts half as long as a 4.0Ah pack. The HART kit includes both sizes, and the DEWALT drill and saw kit has two 2.0Ah packs. A circular saw drains a small pack in minutes. Count batteries per tool. A spare 4.0Ah or 5.0Ah pack is the best first add-on for any kit that ships with 2.0Ah packs.

The battery family decides which tools you can add later. M18 and 20V MAX are broad, while V20 and HART are narrower. A five-year plan matters more than the kit price. Check that the tools you want in two years, such as a sander, a grinder or a vacuum, exist for the platform.

More tools often means lighter-duty tools. The Milwaukee kit uses pro-grade tools, while the seven-tool CRAFTSMAN uses consumer tools. A pro tool lasts years of daily use. The tool in a kit is often a bare-bones version of the standalone model, so compare the model numbers.

A bag keeps tools together. A charger that fills a 2.0Ah pack in under an hour saves downtime. Check that the kit includes a charger and a bag. A bag with a hard base protects tools better than a soft bag when thrown in a truck.

specDecoder.meaning: UWO is the power delivered at the chuck. It is DEWALT's way of describing output.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT's 340 UWO and the CRAFTSMAN's 280 UWO are not comparable with other brands' torque figures. Do not compare UWO against torque in in-lbs, because they measure different things.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp hours measure battery capacity. A larger number runs longer.
specDecoder.watchFor: The HART's 4.0Ah pack runs twice as long as the 2.0Ah pack. A pack's label capacity assumes a fresh, warm cell.

specDecoder.meaning: Brushless motors use electronics instead of brushes. They run cooler and last longer.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not assume every tool in a kit is brushless. Check each tool's own spec, not the kit's headline.

specDecoder.meaning: Torque is the twisting force of the tool. Impact drivers list it in inch-pounds.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT impact driver's 1,500 in-lbs is a peak figure. Impact drivers and drills quote different torque units.

specDecoder.meaning: Tool count is the number of tools in the box. It does not describe their quality.
specDecoder.watchFor: A seven-tool kit is not seven times the value of a one-tool kit. Extra tools often come with lower-spec batteries.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tool mix
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared which tools each kit includes, from the Milwaukee's hammer drill and Hackzall to the CRAFTSMAN's seven tools. The mix decides whether the kit fits the buyer's jobs. We treated tool mix as the first filter and then judged quality within the mix.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor technology
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for brushless motors, which extend runtime. The HART kit leads on this. We checked listing text to see whether brushless applies to every tool.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery value
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted batteries and capacity, noting that circular saws drain small packs. We noted that a circular saw is the hungriest tool in any kit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform breadth
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed the size of each battery family, from M18 to HART. Platform breadth is a long-term factor that kit prices hide.

howWeEvaluated.title: Relative value
howWeEvaluated.description: We used price tier to compare what extra spending buys. We used relative price tiers only and never quoted a listing price.

howToChoose.intro: Choose by the work you actually do and by the battery family you want to own, since the kit's tool count says little about how well each tool performs.
Relative tiers only: moving up a tier here mostly buys brushless motors, a bigger battery and a deeper platform, not extra tools.

cards.label: Big kit
cards.text: Five to seven tools cover most jobs but spread batteries thin. The CRAFTSMAN and DEWALT 5-tool kits fall here.

cards.label: Small kit
cards.text: Two to four tools with stronger components. The Milwaukee, HART and DEWALT drill and saw kits fall here.

howToChoose.note: Whichever size you pick, buy one extra battery for the saw, because a circular saw drains a pack faster than any other tool in the bag.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A deck needs a drill, an impact driver, a circular saw and extra batteries. Brushless saws and large packs matter most. Wet pressure-treated lumber is the hardest load, so plan for spare batteries.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEWALT 5-Tool Kit covers all of them. The Milwaukee kit lacks a circular saw, and the drill and saw kit lacks an impact driver.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use tools weekly or plan to build a collection. The Milwaukee 2695-24 shows where pro-grade platforms begin.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use tools a few times a month. The HART or CRAFTSMAN kit covers that. Wait for a sale on a bare tool if you need a single extra tool later.

maintenance.why: Heat and full charge age cells. Cool storage keeps capacity. Disconnect batteries before long storage.
Dust makes bits slip. Clean jaws hold tight. Brush out the chuck and collet.
Dull blades drain batteries fast. Fresh blades save runtime. Store spare blades in a case.
Dirty contacts waste power. A dry cloth is enough. Check them again after a heavy summer.
Loose tools collect dust and get damaged. A bag protects them. Check that the case latches close.

faq.q: Is a combo kit cheaper than buying tools separately?
faq.a: Usually, yes. A kit includes batteries and a charger, which cost a lot separately. Check the tools you need. A kit also includes a bag and a charger, which add real value.
It buys a multi-tool kit on a pro or consumer platform. Listing prices move, so check the live cost. Expect to add a larger battery as the first accessory.
Pro-grade tools last for years. Batteries usually wear first. Replace batteries when runtime drops, not the tools.
Not necessarily. More tools often means lighter-duty tools. Pick the tools you will use. A kit you use fully beats a kit you half use.
A motor that uses electronics instead of carbon brushes. It runs longer and lasts longer. It also runs quieter and cooler.
M18 and 20V MAX are broadest. V20 and HART are narrower. Choose the family you want in five years. Pro platforms hold their resale value better.
